trigger: rotate via Settings then restart
summary: The rotation runbook this branch added prescribes Settings->OIDC, but that swap is PROCESS-LOCAL. After a restart the provider is rebuilt from CLI/env (the disclosed secret) or not built at all. The remediation for a disclosed credential reverts to the disclosed credential.

trigger: store becomes unreadable AFTER boot
summary: MEASURED against real objects: is_open() is construction-time, so the 503 added for R2 cannot fire post-boot. get_all_with_secrets() swallows the prepare failure and returns empty -> 200 with overrides:{}, i.e. 'never set, nothing to rotate' on the route the runbook depends on. Same root cause as R5: the read API cannot express failure.
adjudication: Split to its own PR by operator decision. Verified NON-REGRESSING: origin/dev has the identical swallow-failure read path (get_all_with_secrets returns an empty vector on a prepare failure) and the identical 200-with-empty-overrides, so this branch does not cause or worsen CH-2 - it improves the boot-time case with a new 503 and leaves the post-boot case as it already shipped. The real fix is making RuntimeConfigStore's read API able to report failure, which also closes R5 (boot with an unreadable store applying zero overrides silently). That is a design change to a store API and warrants its own review round.

trigger: one of six OIDC set() calls fails
summary: No transaction across the six writes. 5-of-6 persisted is reported as 'NOT saved ... will revert on restart' - false in both halves. A single set() measured blocking 5003ms under a foreign exclusive transaction, so one save can hold a worker ~30s.

The R1 false-success shape re-entering through the guard added to remove it.
